faq.q: Why was the Taj Mahal built?
faq.a: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built it as a tomb in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631. Both of them now rest inside.

faq.q: How long did it take to build the Taj Mahal?
faq.a: About 22 years. Work began in 1632, the main tomb was finished around 1643, and the whole complex around 1653.
asks: When was the Taj Mahal finished?

faq.q: Where did the marble for the Taj Mahal come from?
faq.a: From Makrana in Rajasthan. Coloured stones for the inlay came from many places across India and Asia.
asks: What is the Taj Mahal made of?

faq.a: It is the art of cutting coloured stones and setting them into marble to make pictures like flowers and vines. On the Taj Mahal it is also called parchin kari.
asks: How were the flowers on the Taj Mahal made?

faq.q: Why do the minarets lean outwards?
faq.a: They tilt very slightly outwards so that, if one fell in an earthquake, it would fall away from the main tomb.
asks: Are the Taj Mahal towers leaning?

facts: The Taj Mahal was built in Agra, India, from 1632 to about 1653 by order of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
Its white marble came from Makrana in Rajasthan.
The Taj Mahal became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
